history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - Digambara JAIN temple; keep-or-drop decision needed. Main temple of the Champapur Siddha Kshetra at Nathnagar/Champanagar, Bhagalpur, on the site of ancient Champa, capital of the Anga Mahajanapada. Champapuri is claimed to be the only place where all five kalyanas (garbha, janma, diksha, kevalagnana, moksha) of Bhagwan Vasupujya (12th Tirthankara) took place; the temple's five altars symbolise the Panch Kalyanaka. The red Padmasana idol of Vasupujya in the central altar is said to match his actual complexion; an Ashtadhatu idol and ancient foot images (charan) of Vasupujya are also installed. Two of the original four Keerti Stambhas (Columns of Fame, claimed ~2200 years old) survive; two were destroyed in the 1934 earthquake and the remaining two repaired in 1938. A 31-foot-tall statue of Vasupujya is the newest addition. Jain tradition also records monsoon stays of Adinatha, Parshwanatha and Mahavira here. CONFLICTING DATES: jain.org.in dates the main temple to ~2500 years, MakeMyTrip to ~2.5 centuries - verify.

name: Champapur Digambar Jain Mandir
town_description: Bhagalpur, the 'Silk City' of Bihar, sits on the southern bank of the Ganges and is one of the oldest cities of the Gangetic plain - ancient Champa/Champanagar was the capital of the Anga Mahajanapada. It is famous for its tussar silk industry, the Vikramshila Mahavihara ruins at Antichak nearby, and as the home of Tilka Manjhi, an early tribal freedom fighter.
